title: Vanderbilt University Need-Based Financial Aid and Merit Scholarships for International First-Year Undergraduate Applicants
program_type: University-administered need-based grant aid combined with competitive university merit scholarships awarded at admission
funding_type: Need-based institutional gift aid meeting 100% of demonstrated need without loans, plus renewable merit scholarships ranging from partial awards to full tuition plus fees, housing and a summer stipend
administering_authority: Vanderbilt University (Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships)
implementing_agency: Vanderbilt University Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships, with the Office of Undergraduate Admissions administering the MyAppVU scholarship application portal
programme_action: Opportunity Vanderbilt / Vanderbilt University institutional financial aid and scholarship programmes for the four undergraduate schools (College of Arts and Science, Peabody College, School of Engineering, Blair School of Music)
description: Vanderbilt University offers need-based scholarships to a limited number of international first-year undergraduate applicants, and international first-year applicants are eligible to apply for all merit-based scholarships offered at Vanderbilt. International students with demonstrated need who are admitted will have 100% of their demonstrated need met with grants and/or scholarships. Vanderbilt is need-aware for international citizens: requesting need-based aid may be a factor in the final admissions decision, and applications from international citizens who seek need-based aid are reviewed together against academic qualities, leadership and community engagement, financial need, and availability of resources. For international students admitted for fall 2026, Vanderbilt offered need-based aid and/or merit scholarships to 89 students representing 54 countries, with awards ranging from $16,815 to $99,998 per year for four years.

award_types: Need-based scholarships for international students (limited number of first-year applicants)
Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship (signature, full tuition plus one-time summer stipend)
Ingram Scholars Program (signature, full tuition plus all required fees and the value of on-campus housing, plus a summer service project stipend)

Additional merit scholarships: Carell Family Scholarship (full tuition and fees); Clark Scholars Program ($20,000 per year plus summer immersive assistance); Curb Leadership Scholarship ($8,000); Fred Russell-Grantland Rice Scholarship; National Merit Scholarship awards; regional scholarships for Houston, Texas and selected counties in Arkansas, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee

Restricted international awards: Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship (Finland, full tuition plus up to $6,000 summer stipend and $1,500 per year travel allowance); Irene and Thomas Harrington International Scholarship (preference France, then European Union); Early-White International Scholarship (United Kingdom or European Union member countries)
Nashville Vanderbilt Scholars Program and Blair Ovation Award (very high value, but not open to international applicants)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: Need-based aid is the largest source of Vanderbilt student financial assistance and is need-aware for international applicants. Merit scholarships are separate and competitive: for fall 2027 entry the two remaining signature programmes are the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and the Ingram Scholars Program (the Chancellor's Scholarship is no longer offered to applicants from fall 2027 onward). Additional merit awards are identified by the Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships and are open to international applicants.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Vanderbilt need-based scholarships are renewable for up to four years (eight semesters) of full-time enrollment with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 after the freshman year. Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholars renew annually with at least a 3.0 GPA. Ingram Scholars renew annually with a 3.0 minimum GPA plus fulfillment of service-related requirements: approximately twenty hours of community service each month during the academic year and one summer service project following the sophomore year. Merit scholarships generally renew for four years as long as the recipient maintains satisfactory academic performance.
programme_structure.intake: Fall entry only for first-year applicants; the 2027-28 financial aid calendar is published for fall 2027 entry

status_note: Open for the fall 2027 entry cycle as published on 3 October 2026. The Early Decision I admission deadline (1 November 2026) and the merit scholarship application deadline (1 December 2026) are both in the future. Next cycle: fall 2028 entry, with deadlines expected in the same November-February pattern. Note that test-optional policy covers fall 2027 and fall 2028 entry only; SAT or ACT scores are required for fall 2029 entry.
verification_type: Official university pages read directly on vanderbilt.edu and admissions.vanderbilt.edu
verification_notes: Eleven official Vanderbilt pages and one official Vanderbilt PDF were read directly: the Financial Aid International Students page, the Financial Aid Deadlines page (2027-28 calendar), the Costs: On-Campus or Off-Campus page (2026-27 figures), the Merit Scholarship Opportunities hub, the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship page, the Ingram Scholars Program page, the Additional Merit Scholarships page, the Scholarship Application page, the Scholarships FAQ, the Undergraduate Admissions Affordability page, the International Costs and Finances page, the First-year Application Process page, the Types of Financial Assistance page, and the Fall 2027 Merit Application Questions PDF. Two official Vanderbilt statements conflict on the required international financial-aid form: the Financial Aid International Students page states that at the time of submission the only document required is the College Board Financial Aid PROFILE and that Vanderbilt reserves the right to request additional documentation, while the admissions pages state that international applicants requesting need-based aid must submit the CSS Profile or the ISFAA (International Student Financial Aid Application). Both are recorded here; applicants should file the CSS Profile and be prepared to supply the ISFAA and income/tax documentation on request. No 'Vanderbilt International Grant' exists on any current official Vanderbilt page read for this record; the named international awards are those listed in programme_structure.award_types.
source_last_updated: Admissions Dates and Deadlines and the Financial Aid Deadlines page both present a 2027-28 financial aid calendar with 2026 dates, indicating current-cycle publication for fall 2027 entry as of 3 October 2026. The Costs page presents academic year 2026-27 figures. Vanderbilt publishes no explicit 'page last updated' date on these pages.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Merit scholarship applications for fall 2027 entry are due 1 December 2026 under every decision plan. Need-based aid priority filing dates for the CSS Profile / ISFAA are 1 November 2026 (Early Decision I), 1 January 2027 (Early Decision II) and 1 February 2027 (Regular Decision). Admission application deadlines are 1 November 2026 (Early Decision I) and 1 January 2027 (Early Decision II and Regular Decision).
application_deadline.application_period: Fall 2027 entry cycle. The merit scholarship application becomes available in the MyAppVU portal 2-3 business days after the admission application is submitted.
application_deadline.official_rule: Vanderbilt's published FINANCIAL AID CALENDAR 2027-28 states: Early Decision I first-year applicants - 1 November 2026 priority filing deadline for CSS PROFILE and FAFSA; 1 December 2026 deadline for merit scholarship applications. Early Decision II first-year applicants - 1 December 2026 deadline for merit scholarship applications; 1 January 2027 priority filing deadline for CSS PROFILE and FAFSA. Regular Decision first-year - 1 December 2026 deadline for merit scholarship applications; 1 February 2027 priority filing deadline for CSS PROFILE and FAFSA. The Undergraduate Admissions Dates and Deadlines page states the completed application deadlines: Early Decision I 1 November 2026, Early Decision II 1 January 2027, Regular Decision 1 January 2027. The International Costs and Finances page states that the CSS Profile or ISFAA must be submitted by 1 November 2026 for Early Decision I, 1 January 2027 for Early Decision II and 1 February 2027 for Regular Decision.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Vanderbilt publishes no time of day and no time zone for any of these deadlines, so no timezone is asserted here. The 1 December 2026 merit scholarship deadline is the single date common to all three decision plans and is the binding constraint for scholarship consideration; the need-based aid priority dates differ by decision plan. Because merit scholarship recipients are notified only in late March, an international applicant admitted under a binding Early Decision plan must commit to Vanderbilt before learning the merit outcome. Transfer applicants are not eligible for merit scholarships and international transfer applicants who are not U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens are not eligible for need-based aid (such applications are withdrawn).

programme_duration.official_range: Four years of full-time undergraduate study
programme_duration.renewal_note: Need-based scholarship assistance is renewable for a maximum of four years (eight semesters) of full-time enrollment, subject to a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 after the freshman year and satisfactory academic progress. Cornelius Vanderbilt and Ingram Scholars renew annually with a 3.0 GPA; Ingram adds a twenty-hour monthly service commitment and one summer service project.

funding.scholarship_type: Institutional need-based grant aid (gift aid, no loans) plus competitive university merit scholarships awarded at admission
funding.monthly_amount_note: Vanderbilt publishes no monthly stipend for international students. Award figures are published as annual amounts: the range for international students admitted for fall 2026 was $16,815-$99,998 per year for four years. The Ingram and Cornelius Vanderbilt summer experiences are paid as a one-time summer stipend, not a monthly allowance.
funding.travel_amount_note: A published annual travel allowance of $1,500 to and from Finland exists only within the Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship, which is restricted to students from Finland enrolled in the College of Arts and Science. No travel allowance is published for the general international need-based or merit programmes; Vanderbilt's affordability guidance states that students should also allow for travel expenses and health insurance.
funding.institutional_costs: Vanderbilt provides all scholarship support as institutional funds; no per-student institutional cost contribution is charged.
funding.fully_funded_note: Vanderbilt states that international students with demonstrated need who are admitted will have 100% of their demonstrated need met with grants and/or scholarships, and that merit scholarship recipients with demonstrated need beyond the scholarship amount will have 100% of that need met as well. The no-loan policy and need-blind admission are stated for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens; for international citizens Vanderbilt is need-aware and meets demonstrated need for those it admits and aids. The top merit awards are not by themselves full-cost awards: the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship covers full tuition plus a one-time summer stipend, and the Ingram Scholars Program covers full tuition, all required fees and the value of on-campus housing plus a summer service stipend. Full cost of attendance is only reached through the combination of a merit award and need-based aid, or through the narrow full-cost awards (Nashville Vanderbilt Scholars, Blair Ovation) that are not open to international applicants.

tuition.conditions: 2026-27 published tuition per year. The Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and the Ingram Scholars Program both cover full tuition; the Carell Family Scholarship covers full tuition and fees.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. Vanderbilt publishes annual award amounts, not a monthly stipend.

travel_allowance.conditions: Published only for the Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship ($1,500 per year as a travel allowance to and from Finland, plus a one-time stipend of up to $6,000 for summer study abroad, research or another approved experience). No travel allowance is published for the general international programmes.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. No visa or immigration cost support is described on the official pages read.

insurance.note: Not published as a scholarship benefit. Participation in the Vanderbilt-sponsored health insurance plan is mandatory unless the online insurance waiver is submitted by 15 July, and students are told to allow for health insurance costs.

book_allowance.note: Not published in official source. A books, course materials, supplies and equipment allowance of $1,100 is included in the 2026-27 cost of attendance as an indirect cost, but no book stipend is published for international students.

accommodation_support.conditions: 2026-27 published housing cost per year. The Ingram Scholars Program explicitly covers the value of on-campus housing each year. Housing is covered for other international students only insofar as it forms part of demonstrated need met at 100%.

bond.note: No bond or service obligation is attached to the need-based award or to the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship. The Ingram Scholars Program carries a continuing service requirement (approximately twenty hours per month during the academic year and one summer service project after the sophomore year), not a financial bond.

total_estimated_value.conditions: This is the 2026-27 total direct cost of attendance at Vanderbilt ($96,896) plus total indirect costs ($3,098). It is a cost-of-attendance figure, not an award amount. The published award range for international students admitted for fall 2026 was $16,815-$99,998 per year for four years.

coverage: Housing (2026-27: $15,170 per year) for Ingram Scholars and, for other aided students, to the extent housing is part of demonstrated need met at 100%
Food (2026-27: $8,520 per year) within demonstrated need met at 100%
Student support fee (2026-27: $3,384 per year), explicitly covered for Ingram Scholars
100% of demonstrated financial need met with grants and/or scholarships, without loans, for admitted international students who apply
One-time summer stipend for an immersive experience following the sophomore or junior year (Cornelius Vanderbilt, Ingram, and the high-value awards)
Travel allowance of $1,500 per year to and from Finland (Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship, Finland-restricted only)
Cash grants beginning from $8,000 per year for additional merit scholarships, and $20,000 per year for the Clark Scholars Program
coverage_limitations: Need-based aid for international students is offered to a limited number of first-year applicants and is need-aware: requesting aid may be a factor in the admissions decision.
No need-based aid is available for international transfer applicants who are not U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens; those applications are withdrawn on receipt.
Merit scholarships are not available to transfer applicants of any citizenship.
Roughly 1% of the entire freshman applicant pool is offered a merit-based scholarship, and the number of awards is limited because most Vanderbilt assistance is need-based.

The Ingram Scholars Program carries a continuing service commitment (about twenty hours per month during the academic year plus one summer service project after the sophomore year), so it is not an unconditional full-tuition award.

Three named international awards restrict eligibility by nationality: the Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship (Finland), the Irene and Thomas Harrington International Scholarship (preference France, then European Union) and the Early-White International Scholarship (United Kingdom or European Union member countries).

Several additional merit awards restrict eligibility by residence: the Nashville Vanderbilt Scholars Program (Metro Nashville Public Schools), regional scholarships for Houston, Texas and selected counties in Arkansas, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee, and National Merit awards which are practically limited to students in the U.S. programme.
No travel, installation, insurance, book or visa support is published for the general international need-based or merit programmes.
Vanderbilt publishes no monthly allowance; published figures are annual amounts and 2026-27 cost-of-attendance figures, and modest annual cost increases should be expected.
The exact benefit structure for an individual student depends on demonstrated need, the award offered, and the undergraduate school, and may differ from the aggregate figures published here.
The two highest-value awards (Nashville Vanderbilt Scholars Program and Blair Ovation Award, each about $97,000) are not open to international applicants.
eligible_applicants: International first-year (freshman) applicants to Vanderbilt University who are not U.S. citizens and not eligible non-citizens for federal student aid purposes
International students seeking need-based scholarships, who must indicate on the admission application that they are seeking need-based assistance
International first-year applicants seeking merit scholarships, who must submit the scholarship application in the MyAppVU portal
Applicants admitted to any of the four undergraduate schools: College of Arts and Science, Peabody College, School of Engineering, and Blair School of Music
U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens living abroad, who are eligible for need-blind admission and the full no-loan need-based programme
final_year_condition: Applicants must be completing secondary school / high school; the requirement is an official high school transcript covering all high school classes and grades to date. Submitting only leaving examination results will not complete the application, so final-year students whose leaving examinations have not yet been sat are still expected to submit full transcripts.
equivalent_degree_note: Vanderbilt has no minimum coursework requirements and uses holistic review. Applicants with non-U.S. secondary qualifications are evaluated within the context of their own system; most successful candidates present the equivalent of five academic subjects each year for four years. Recommended coursework is 4 units of English, 4 units of mathematics, 4 units of natural science, 2 units of foreign language, 2 units of social science or humanities and 4 units of additional work. Applicants to the School of Engineering are strongly recommended to have taken calculus, calculus-based physics and chemistry.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published on the official Vanderbilt pages read for this record.

nationality_quota: No official quota is published. Vanderbilt reports that for international students admitted for fall 2026 it offered need-based aid and/or merit scholarships to 89 students representing 54 countries. Roughly 1% of the entire freshman applicant pool is offered a merit-based scholarship. Applications from international citizens who apply for need-based assistance are reviewed among all international applicants seeking need-based assistance.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to all nationalities. For financial aid purposes an international student is one who does not meet the eligibility criteria to receive federal student financial assistance or is not classified as an eligible non-citizen. U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens (including those living abroad) are treated as domestic applicants with need-blind admission and no-loan need-based aid.
eligibility.residence_requirement: None for the general international need-based and merit programmes. Residence-based restrictions apply only to specific awards: Nashville Vanderbilt Scholars Program (Metro Nashville Public Schools students), regional scholarships (Houston, Texas and selected counties in Arkansas, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee), and the Finland, France/European Union, United Kingdom/European Union restricted awards.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: An official high school transcript including all high school classes and grades or marks to date is required. Submitting only leaving examinations will not complete the application.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Holistic review with no standardized testing or GPA cutoffs for admission. Candidates must excel within the highly selective admissions review. Recommended curriculum and rigor are described above. Merit scholarship recipients are typically in the top 1% of their high school class in rigorous programmes.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA for admission. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 is required to renew University need-based scholarship funds after the freshman year; the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and the Ingram Scholars Program require a 3.0 GPA for annual renewal.
eligibility.language_requirement: English proficiency results are required if applicable. Recommended minimums published: TOEFL iBT 5, TOEFL Essentials 10.5, IELTS 7.0, Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185, LanguageCert 75, Duolingo English Test 130. Exemptions apply for applicants whose first language or language of instruction is English, or who score above 26 on the ACT English section or above 630 on the SAT Evidence-based Reading and Writing section.
eligibility.work_experience: Not a general requirement. Part-time employment during high school years is the specific qualifying criterion for the Carell Family Scholarship.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Strong co-curricular engagement is central to both admission and merit selection. Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholars are selected on academic achievement, intellectual promise, and leadership and contribution outside the classroom. Ingram Scholars are selected on commitment to civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, strength of personal character and leadership potential.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Leadership and contribution outside the classroom are explicit selection factors for the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship; leadership potential is an explicit factor for the Ingram Scholars Program.
eligibility.financial_need: Required for need-based aid, and determined from the CSS Profile or ISFAA. Financial need is not a factor in merit scholarship selection unless the award states otherwise: the Carell Family Scholarship and the Clark Scholars Program both require demonstrated financial need.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time enrollment as a first-year entering student. Vanderbilt aid programmes provide assistance for a maximum of four years (eight semesters) of full-time enrollment toward a first baccalaureate degree.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health or disability restriction is published. Participation in the Vanderbilt-sponsored health insurance plan is mandatory unless the online insurance waiver is submitted by 15 July.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None for most merit scholarships; no merit scholarship awarded to incoming first-year students is designated for a specific major, although the majority are identified with a particular undergraduate school. The Fred Russell-Grantland Rice Scholarship is for students interested in a career in sports journalism, and the Clark Scholars Program serves meritorious engineering undergraduates.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage or fixed mark threshold is published for admission or for the general need-based programme. The only published academic thresholds are the renewal GPA requirements (2.00 for need-based funds after the freshman year; 3.0 for the Cornelius Vanderbilt and Ingram signature awards) and the English proficiency recommended minimum scores.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Recommended coursework: 4 units English, 4 units mathematics, 4 units natural science, 2 units foreign language, 2 units social science/humanities, 4 units additional academic work. Engineering applicants should have taken calculus, calculus-based physics and chemistry. SAT or ACT scores are optional for fall 2027 and fall 2028 entry and required for fall 2029 entry. English proficiency recommended minimums: TOEFL iBT 5, TOEFL Essentials 10.5, IELTS 7.0, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185, LanguageCert 75, Duolingo English Test 130.
selection_factors_may_include: Academic record and rigor of coursework
Leadership and contribution outside the classroom
Financial need (need-based awards and need-based additional merit awards)
Personal essay and required short answer
Audition scores for Blair School of Music applicants
Summer stipend or service project proposal (signature awards)
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Vanderbilt states that it uses a holistic admissions review process and does not employ cutoffs for standardized testing or grade point averages. Demonstrated interest is not considered. For international applicants, aid applications are reviewed among all international applicants seeking need-based assistance and are chosen on an evaluation of academic qualities, leadership and community engagement, financial need, and availability of resources.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Applicants whose first language or language of instruction is English are not required to submit English proficiency exam scores. Applicants scoring above 26 on the ACT English section or above 630 on the SAT Evidence-based Reading and Writing section are also exempt.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The published values are labelled by Vanderbilt as 'Recommended minimum score' and are not cutoffs. Transcribed exactly: TOEFL iBT 5; TOEFL Essentials 10.5; IELTS 7.0; Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185; LanguageCert 75; Duolingo English Test 130. Note that the TOEFL iBT figure of 5 is not on the legacy 0-120 scale and appears to reflect a rescaled TOEFL score, so applicants should confirm current scales directly with ETS and Vanderbilt. English proficiency exams must be sent from a testing agency or high school official directly and will not be superscored.
accepted_tests: TOEFL iBT (including Home and Paper Editions)

language_of_instruction.language_note: All instruction is in English and all application pieces must be provided in English. Transcripts and recommendation letters not originally in English must be officially translated by the high school or a certified translator; applicants may not provide their own translation. An EducationUSA advising office can assist with translation.

application_method.application_route: Direct application to Vanderbilt through the Common Application, Coalition powered by Scoir, or QuestBridge; the merit scholarship application is then completed through the MyAppVU portal, and the CSS Profile or ISFAA is submitted through the College Board portal.
application_steps: Submit the admission application through the Common Application, Coalition powered by Scoir, or QuestBridge (submit through only one system), including the personal essay and short answer, by the decision-plan deadline (Early Decision I 1 November 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision 1 January 2027).
Indicate on the admission application whether you are seeking need-based financial assistance; this makes the admissions review need-aware for international applicants.

Complete the international section of the Common Application, send official English proficiency results if applicable, and submit an official high school transcript covering all classes and grades to date.
Arrange the counselor letter of recommendation and two academic teacher letters of recommendation.
Within 2-3 business days of submitting the admission application, create the MyAppVU account from the email sent by the Office of Undergraduate Admissions.

Submit the merit scholarship application(s) in the MyAppVU portal under the Scholarship Application tab, uploading responses as PDF or Word only, by 1 December 2026. Applying for the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application is required for consideration and is also the recommended route for the Additional Merit Scholarships.

Submit the College Board CSS Profile or the ISFAA (International Student Financial Aid Application) by the decision-plan priority deadline: 1 November 2026 (ED I), 1 January 2027 (ED II), 1 February 2027 (RD).
Supply any additional documentation Vanderbilt requests to verify information submitted on the PROFILE or ISFAA.
application_method.application_fee: USD 50 nonrefundable application fee, or a fee waiver for qualified students. Vanderbilt accepts all application fee waiver requests submitted through the Coalition and Common Applications for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens, and the fee is automatically waived for QuestBridge applicants; no fee-waiver route is published specifically for international applicants.

selection_process.decision_maker: Vanderbilt University Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships, with the Office of Undergraduate Admissions conducting the holistic admissions review; Ingram Scholars are selected by a dedicated selection committee
selection_process.selection_type: Holistic, need-aware for international citizens; competitive merit review based on the full admission application plus the scholarship application
possible_stages: Submission of the admission application and all required materials
Review of international citizens seeking need-based assistance among all international applicants seeking need-based assistance
Merit scholarship review in February and March, based on the entire admission application plus the scholarship application
Finalist interview for Ingram Scholars (finalists are required to interview with the selection committee)
Notification: preliminary financial aid offers mid-December (ED I) or mid-February (ED II), final offers late March; merit scholarship recipients notified late March
selection_process.weighting_note: Vanderbilt publishes no numeric weighting for any admission or scholarship criterion. Selection is described as holistic with no cutoffs for testing or GPA.
selection_process.results_timing: Early Decision I: preliminary financial aid offers mid-December 2026, updated offers late March 2027, admission decisions mid-December 2026. Early Decision II and Regular Decision: preliminary offers mid-February 2027 (ED II), late March 2027 (all plans) for final offers and admission decisions. Merit scholarship recipients are notified by mail and e-mail in late March 2027; only recipients are notified.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: The waitlist is not ranked. Merit scholarships are not re-awarded to other students if a recipient declines, because Vanderbilt over-awards relative to expected enrollment.

selection_criteria.academic_excellence: Central. Merit scholarship recipients are usually in the top 1% of their high school class in rigorous academic programmes, and typically score in the mid-1500s on the SAT and/or above 34 on the ACT, though only about half of applicants with scores in those ranges receive merit offers.
selection_criteria.leadership: Explicit selection factor for the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and for the Ingram Scholars Program (leadership potential).
selection_criteria.community_service: Explicit selection factor for the Ingram Scholars Program (commitment to civic-minded service) and for the need-based international review (leadership and community engagement).
selection_criteria.extracurricular_achievement: Explicit. Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholars are selected on academic achievement, intellectual promise, and leadership and contribution outside the classroom; Ingram Scholars on civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, personal character and leadership potential.
selection_criteria.financial_need: Required for need-based aid and for the need-based additional merit awards (Carell Family Scholarship, Clark Scholars Program). Not a factor in merit scholarship selection unless the award states otherwise.
additional_factors: Audition scores for Blair School of Music applicants
Part-time employment during high school years (Carell Family Scholarship)
Interest in a career in sports journalism (Fred Russell-Grantland Rice Scholarship)
Creativity and community transformation (Curb Leadership Scholarship)
Nationality or residence for the restricted international and regional awards
selection_criteria.interview_required: Partial. Ingram Scholar finalists are required to interview with the selection committee. Vanderbilt does not conduct admission interviews, but optional InitialView video interviews are available to international applicants.
selection_criteria.portfolio_required: Blair School of Music applicants only: prescreening video, music resume and repertoire list. A Schoolhouse.world portfolio may optionally be uploaded via MyAppVU.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from the admitting undergraduate school of Vanderbilt University
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Four years (eight semesters) of full-time study
possible_awards: Bachelor of Science degrees in the School of Engineering
degree_outcome.degree_note: Need-based assistance supports students pursuing their first baccalaureate degree for a maximum of four years (eight semesters) of full-time enrollment. Vanderbilt awards college credit for AP scores of 4 or 5 and IB scores of 6 or 7, though required scores vary by exam.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: AP credit is granted for a score of 4 or 5 and IB credit for 6 or 7, with required scores varying by exam per the Undergraduate Catalog and Registrar's advanced credit and course placement guidance.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full tuition is covered by the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship, the Ingram Scholars Program and the Carell Family Scholarship; 100% of demonstrated need is met for admitted international students who apply, up to the full cost of attendance.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: USD 50 application fee for all applicants, waivable through the Common and Coalition Applications for qualified students and automatically waived for QuestBridge applicants. No fee-waiver route specific to international applicants is published.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Early Decision I and II are binding plans requiring the applicant, a parent or guardian, and the high school counselor to sign the Early Decision Agreement and to withdraw all other applications if admitted. Merit scholarships are renewed subject to satisfactory academic performance, and Ingram Scholars must maintain a twenty-hour monthly service commitment and complete one summer service project.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: On-campus housing and dining, library, Student Employment (up to 19 hours per week on campus, with most undergraduate students awarded $1,000-$2,700 per year where work-study applies), the Critical Support Fund, and the VUSE laptop loaner programme.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No financial bond applies. Failure to maintain the renewal criteria ends the award: a cumulative GPA below 2.00 after the freshman year ends University need-based scholarship renewal, a GPA below 3.0 ends the Cornelius Vanderbilt and Ingram awards, and failure to meet Ingram service requirements ends the Ingram award.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you meet the definition of an international student for aid purposes (not a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen)
Choose one application platform only: Common Application, Coalition powered by Scoir, or QuestBridge
Decide the decision plan; Early Decision I and II are binding
Book the English proficiency test early if required, since results must be sent directly by the testing agency and are not superscored
Request the counselor recommendation and two academic teacher letters of recommendation well in advance
Ask the high school or a certified translator for official English translations of transcripts and recommendations
File the CSS Profile or ISFAA in time for the decision-plan priority deadline
Watch for the MyAppVU email within 2-3 business days of submitting the admission application and complete the merit scholarship application by 1 December 2026
Upload scholarship responses as PDF or Word and confirm the green check mark within 24 hours
Budget for the $400 matriculation deposit (waived automatically for international students receiving a need-based aid award) and for health insurance and travel costs
programme_comparison_fields: Share of cost covered (tuition only vs tuition, fees and housing)
Whether demonstrated need must also be shown
Whether additional need-based aid stacks on top
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and Ingram Scholars Program applications are reviewed alongside the entire admission application, so the scholarship responses should extend rather than repeat the personal essay and short answer. Lead with concrete, verifiable contribution: leadership you exercised, community problems you engaged with and outcomes you produced. For Ingram, make the service record, the entrepreneurial quality of the work and the sustainability of the commitment explicit, because finalists must interview and explain a twenty-hour monthly commitment. For the Additional Merit Scholarships, answer the scholarship-specific questions for the Carell Family Scholarship (part-time employment during high school plus demonstrated need), Clark Scholars Program (engineering with demonstrated need) and Curb Leadership Scholarship (creativity at the center of your life and community transformation).
profile_fit_labels: Top-percent academic record in a rigorous curriculum
Applicant from Finland, France, the United Kingdom or the European Union (restricted awards)
common_mistakes: Assuming aid is automatic: applying for admission does not apply you for aid. The CSS Profile or ISFAA must be filed separately by the decision-plan deadline.
Missing the 1 December 2026 merit scholarship deadline, which is the same under all decision plans and the deadline for the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application.
Submitting only leaving examination results instead of a full official transcript.
Self-translating transcripts or recommendation letters; translations must come from the school or a certified translator.
Failing to upload scholarship answers as PDF or Word in MyAppVU, or submitting corrections after the fact; post-submission corrections are not accepted.
Not checking for the green check mark confirming scholarship submission within 24 hours.
Applying through more than one application platform.
Assuming a need-based award stacks on top of a merit scholarship without applying for need-based aid.
Applying as a transfer applicant expecting merit aid or, for non-citizen internationals, need-based aid.
Committing under a binding Early Decision plan without knowing the merit outcome, which is not released until late March.

risk_flags.risk: Need-aware admission for international citizens means requesting need-based aid can reduce the chance of admission.
risk_flags.impact: An otherwise competitive international applicant may be denied admission specifically because they requested aid.
risk_flags.mitigation: Recognize the trade-off explicitly. Vanderbilt states international applicants with demonstrated need who are admitted have 100% of need met, so an applicant with genuine need should still apply, but should not assume aid availability influences only funding.

risk_flags.risk: Merit scholarships are awarded to roughly 1% of the applicant pool and are not re-awarded if declined.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants cannot rely on a merit award, and a declined award is not redistributed.
risk_flags.mitigation: Always apply for need-based aid as well; Vanderbilt explicitly encourages this because merit awards alone rarely cover full cost.

risk_flags.risk: Timing conflict between the binding Early Decision plans and the late March merit notification.
risk_flags.impact: An ED-admitted international applicant must enrol before learning whether a merit scholarship was awarded.
risk_flags.mitigation: Choose Regular Decision if comparing aid packages, as Vanderbilt encourages, unless fully committed to Vanderbilt regardless of the merit outcome.

risk_flags.risk: Inconsistent official statements about the required international financial-aid form (CSS Profile only versus CSS Profile or ISFAA).
risk_flags.impact: An applicant may omit the ISFAA and be asked for it later, or may believe the ISFAA replaces the CSS Profile.
risk_flags.mitigation: File the CSS Profile as the primary form by the decision-plan deadline, and keep the ISFAA and income documentation ready to supply on request, as Vanderbilt reserves the right to request additional documentation.

risk_flags.risk: The published English proficiency minimums appear to be on rescaled instruments (for example TOEFL iBT 5) and are labelled 'recommended'.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant may prepare to the wrong scale or treat a recommended minimum as a cutoff.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm current score scales with ETS, Cambridge, LanguageCert and Duolingo, and meet or exceed the published figures. Scores must be sent directly from the testing agency and are not superscored.

risk_flags.risk: The Chancellor's Scholarship was discontinued for applicants from fall 2027 while some official pages still list it as a signature award.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant may target a scholarship that no longer exists for their entry year.
risk_flags.mitigation: For fall 2027 entry, target only the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and the Ingram Scholars Program, which replace it at approximately 225 signature awards in total. Existing Chancellor's Scholarship holders continue through graduation.

risk_flags.risk: Cost of attendance is high (2026-27 direct costs of $96,896) and Vanderbilt states modest annual increases should be expected.
risk_flags.impact: A package that meets 100% of demonstrated need in the entry year may not cover a later, higher cost of attendance.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the published figures as current-cycle only and expect re-assessment each year; note that the maximum assistance window is four years (eight semesters) of full-time enrollment.

risk_flags.risk: Nationality-restricted and residence-restricted awards can mislead applicants into assuming general eligibility.
risk_flags.impact: Time spent pursuing the Hilppa A. K. Roby, Harrington or Early-White awards from a non-qualifying country, or the Nashville, Houston and regional awards from outside those areas, is wasted.
risk_flags.mitigation: Screen these awards against nationality and residence before relying on them, and treat the general need-based and Cornelius Vanderbilt / Ingram programmes as the realistic international routes.

best_fit: Strong international first-year applicants with genuine demonstrated financial need and an exceptional academic and co-curricular record who can submit the merit scholarship application by 1 December 2026 and the CSS Profile or ISFAA by their decision-plan deadline, and who accept that requesting aid makes the admissions review need-aware.
not_best_fit: Transfer applicants, who are ineligible for merit scholarships and, if international non-citizens, ineligible for need-based aid
Applicants who need certainty about merit funding before committing under a binding Early Decision plan

Applicants who cannot fund any part of the cost independently, since need is met by a package that also includes an academic year student contribution of up to about $2,700 per year and a work expectation

Applicants seeking a named award restricted to Finland, France, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Metro Nashville Public Schools, or Houston and selected Southern counties who do not meet those nationality or residence criteria
Applicants looking for a research stipend, monthly living allowance, installation grant, visa support or book allowance; none of these is published for the general international programmes
Graduate, doctoral or one-semester exchange applicants

database_notes: No substitution was required: Vanderbilt University international undergraduate aid and merit scholarships are not on the do-not-duplicate list, and the target region (United States) is allowed.

This is a composite record. Vanderbilt publishes no single collective award name covering both need-based aid and merit scholarships for international first-year applicants, so the title is a descriptive construction drawn from the official wording on the International Costs and Finances page. The short_title 'Vanderbilt International Aid' is a constructed short form, not an official acronym, because no real short form is published.

The brief asked to verify a 'Vanderbilt International Grant'. No award of that name appears on any official Vanderbilt page read for this record. The named international awards that do exist are the Hilppa A. K. Roby Scholarship, the Irene and Thomas Harrington International Scholarship and the Early-White International Scholarship, all of which are nationality-restricted; none is a general international grant.

Need-based aid IS open to international students, contrary to the framing in the brief that internationals are excluded: the official pages state that international students with demonstrated need who are admitted will have 100% of demonstrated need met with grants and/or scholarships, and that 89 students from 54 countries received need-based aid and/or merit scholarships for fall 2026. The correct nuance is that the number of awards is limited and the process is need-aware, not that internationals receive no need-based aid. Need-blind admission and the no-loan policy are stated by Vanderbilt for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens.

The official Financial Aid International Students page states that at submission 'the only document we require is the PROFILE' and that Vanderbilt reserves the right to ask for additional documentation, while the admissions pages state that international applicants requesting need-based aid must submit 'the CSS Profile ... or the ISFAA (International Student Financial Aid Application)'. Both statements are quoted verbatim in the record; applicants should file the CSS Profile and be ready to supply the ISFAA plus income documentation on request.

The Chancellor's Scholarship was discontinued for applicants from fall 2027, but the Affordability page still lists it as one of three signature full-tuition awards. The Scholarships FAQ is treated as authoritative for the fall 2027 cycle; the resulting signature awards are the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship and the Ingram Scholars Program only.

Two figures for the total number of merit scholarships appear in official sources: 'about 300 merit-based scholarships to incoming first-year students' on the Affordability page and 'approximately 225 awards' plus 'over 225 recipients ... guaranteed full-tuition awards' on the Scholarships pages. Both are recorded; neither is treated as definitive.

All cost figures are 2026-27 academic year figures (tuition $69,822; housing $15,170; food $8,520; student support fee $3,384; total direct $96,896; books $1,100; personal $1,998; total indirect $3,098). Vanderbilt states that modest annual increases can be expected and that transportation varies. These are cost-of-attendance figures, not award amounts, and are not presented as an award total.

The award range of $16,815-$99,998 per year for four years is the published Vanderbilt figure for international students admitted for fall 2026, not a guaranteed minimum or maximum for any individual applicant.

The need-based package includes an Academic Year Student Contribution of up to about $2,700 per academic year and a work expectation, so '100% of demonstrated need met' does not mean a fully grant-funded education with no student contribution. This is stated in the not_best_fit list.

deadline_date is set to 2026-12-01, the merit scholarship application deadline, because it is the single date common to all three decision plans and the binding constraint for scholarship consideration. The need-based aid priority deadlines (2026-11-01, 2027-01-01, 2027-02-01) and the admission application deadlines (2026-11-01, 2027-01-01) are recorded verbatim in official_rule and typical_application_window. deadline_timezone is null because Vanderbilt publishes no time zone or time of day.

The English proficiency minimums are transcribed exactly as published, including TOEFL iBT 5, which is not on the legacy 0-120 scale and appears to reflect a rescaled instrument. Vanderbilt labels the whole table 'Recommended minimum score', so none of these figures is a cutoff.

Merit scholarship application materials are submitted only through the MyAppVU portal in PDF or Word format, and post-submission corrections are not accepted; the green check mark must appear within 24 hours.

An official logo was located and verified on Vanderbilt's own domains: https://cdn.vanderbilt.edu/vu-futurevu/static/img/favicons/favicon-on-light.png, the site icon declared in the head of https://www.vanderbilt.edu/ (HTTP 200, image/png, valid PNG signature, 32x32). The equivalent https://www.vanderbilt.edu/favicon.ico is a valid 16x16 ICO also returning HTTP 200. No photograph was sourced, so image_url is null.

No top-level key required by the schema contract was omitted, and no unsupported top-level key was added. Amounts are published only where Vanderbilt publishes them; null is used where the official source publishes no figure.
